(2) The policy for the Development of Child-Friendly Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) contains:

b. Children's rights; and
c. the approach to developing Child-Friendly Regency.

CHAPTER IV
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


Part One Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 56
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities to Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
(3) In the event that a Child victim of an act of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence shall be provided formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the educational unit and coordinated with the Women and Child Empowerment Unit

Article 36
(1) Accompaniment services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (3) letter d are carried out for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
(2) In providing accompaniment services as referred to in paragraph (1) P2TP2A may cooperate with persons or institutions that have expertise to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy.

1.3.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation explicitly mentions physical violence (kekerasan fisik). For example, Pasal 5 huruf c states women have the right to protection from “kekerasan fisik, psikologis, seksual, dan penelantaran,” and Pasal 6 huruf d states the same for children. Even within the retrieved English candidates, Article 31(1)(c) says curative care cures illness “physically and psychologically,” and Article 31(3) references victims of violence and includes “Visum et Repertum,” which is typically tied to documenting physical injury. The judge was overly strict in requiring the exact phrase ‘physical violence’ in the retrieved snippets and failed to infer/recognize that the policy covers physical harm/physical aspects of violence in the provided evidence.

1.4.evaluator_rationale: The passages discuss psychological recovery and counseling services, but do not explicitly reference psychological violence itself in the provided excerpts for this criterion.

CHAPTER IV

Part One Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

CHAPTER VIII
CHILD-FRIENDLY REGENCY
Article 68
(1) In order to fulfill Children's rights in an integrated, systematic and sustainable manner, the Regional Government establishes a policy for the Development of Child-Friendly Regency.
(2) The policy for the Development of Child-Friendly Regency as referred to in paragraph (1) contains:
a. the concept of Child-Friendly Regency concerning objectives, strategies and roles of related parties;
b. Children's rights; and
c. the approach to developing Child-Friendly Regency.

Article 9
(1) Obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
(2) Ninik mamak, alim ulama and cadiak pandai as well as bundo kanduang are responsible for protecting and preventing violations of the rights of women and children.
(3) The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 58
(1) Children with disabilities and Children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, nonformal and informal education services, including inclusive education programs.
(2) Regional governments provide teaching staff for inclusive education at every education unit.

1.6.rationale: The policy does address practices commonly treated as harmful practices in VAW/child protection frameworks, specifically child marriage and unregistered marriage. Pasal 24 huruf d requires the community to prevent “pernikahan di bawah tangan dan perkawinan pada usia anak,” and Pasal 11(1) huruf e obligates parents to prevent marriage at child age. Given the document explicitly targets these practices as prevention measures, a ‘Yes’ is defensible; thus the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect for this indicator.

1.9.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly includes protection from sexual exploitation as a right of every woman.

CHAPTER IX
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 72
(1) Regional Government is obligated to conduct guidance and supervision of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. formulation of policies and regulations to be used as guidelines and standards in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection; b. technical guidance and training, includes:
1. providing training for government officials and law enforcement regarding prevention and handling of violence;
2. providing training for religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against women and children;
3. providing training to health workers who provide health services to women and child victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units and general hospitals;
4. providing training to social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect women and child victims of violence; and
5. providing training to PUG working groups and focal points of each Regional Apparatus for the preparation of activity programs based on gender responsive planning and budgeting.
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure in implementing women's empowerment and child protection.
d. facilitation of the formation of nagari that care for women and children; e. provision of information through print and electronic media related to the protection of women and children. (3) Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes: a. monitoring implemented in the form of submission of reports on the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs by the Head of Regional Apparatus to the Regent periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months; and b. evaluation of the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months conducted by the relevant Regional Apparatus (4) The results of supervision as referred to in paragraph (3) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's empowerment and child protection programs.
(5) Further provisions regarding Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 66
(1) Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving Children in the worst forms of work.
(2) The worst forms of work referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. all work in the form of slavery or similar practices;
b. all work that utilizes, provides, or offers Children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances, or gambling;
c. all work that utilizes, provides, or involves Children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances; and/or
d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of Children.

a. the concept of Child-Friendly Regency concerning objectives, strategies and roles of related parties;
b. Children's rights; and
c. the approach to developing Child-Friendly Regency.

Paragraph 2
Obligations Towards Child Protection

1.9.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly includes sexual exploitation as a protected-against harm. Pasal 5 huruf b states women have the right to protection from “eksploitasi ekonomi dan eksploitasi seksual,” and Pasal 6 huruf c provides the same for children. Since the policy directly mentions sexual exploitation, the predicted ‘Yes’ aligns with the source text; the golden label ‘No’ appears wrong.

(2) In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out under one roof, UPTD PPA is responsible for implementing the entire process in one unit to provide the services needed by women and children experiencing problems.
(3) In the event that the implementation of UPTD PPA services as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in a networked manner, UPTD PPA is responsible for the entire referral process for services needed by women and children experiencing problems.
(4) Every element within the UPTD PPA environment in carrying out its duties must apply the principles of coordination, integration, synchronization, accountability and transparency, both within the UPTD PPA environment, as well as in relations between Regional Apparatus, relevant agencies, and community elements.

Part Six
Enhancement of the Role, Quality, and Capability of Women in the Social Sector

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency.
5. Social Service, Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning, hereinafter referred to as the Service, is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Implementation of Women's and Children's Protection.
6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.
8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja Gender Mainstreaming, is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.
9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
10. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
13. Children's Forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
14. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
15. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is action by apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence.
25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
29. Customs are eternal and hereditary codes of conduct from one generation to another generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with the behavioral patterns of society.

Third Part
Effectiveness of Services for Women and Children
Paragraph 1 General

Article 35
(1) Spiritual guidance as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) letter c aims for psychological recovery. (2) Spiritual guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented based on the principles of:
a. not imposing any religion or belief; andb. leaving the final decision in the hands of the victim (selfdetermination).
(3) Spiritual guidance is conducted by spiritual guidance officers.

Article 66
(1) Every person/entity is prohibited from employing and involving Children in the worst forms of work.
(2) The worst forms of work referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. all work in the form of slavery or similar practices;
b. all work that utilizes, provides, or offers Children for prostitution, pornography production, pornographic performances, or gambling;
c. all work that utilizes, provides, or involves Children for the production and trade of alcoholic beverages, narcotics, psychotropic substances, and other addictive substances; and/or
d. all work that endangers the health, safety, or morals of Children.

3.10.rationale: The regulation contains explicit economic support/empowerment measures for women. Pasal 22 includes facilitation of business capital for economically weak women (“fasilitasi penguatan modal usaha”), marketing support, and entrepreneurship training. These are concrete economic support services (even if framed as empowerment rather than victim compensation). Therefore the predicted ‘Yes’ is supported by the Indonesian text, and the golden label ‘No’ likely reflects an overly narrow interpretation.

29. Customs are eternal and hereditary codes of conduct from one generation to another generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with the behavioral patterns of society.

Fourth Part
Obligations of Family and/or Parents Paragraph 1 Obligations Toward the Protection of Women

Seventh Part
Enhancement of the Role, Quality, and Capability of Women in the Economic Field

Article 56
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities to Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
(3) In the event that a Child victim of an act of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence shall be provided formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the educational unit and coordinated with the Women and Child Empowerment Unit

6.3.rationale: The regulation explicitly addresses women in relation to work/employment rights and protections. Pasal 5 huruf d-e recognize rights to decent work and paid leave, and huruf g provides special protection in the implementation of work/profession related to women’s reproductive function. This is a targeted recognition of women workers’ rights/protections. Therefore the predicted ‘Yes’ is supported by the Indonesian text, and the golden label ‘No’ appears wrong (unless the gold intended a much narrower definition, which is not stated here).

Article 64
The Regional Government is obligated to provide Social Welfare for:
a. children in conflict with the law; b. child victims of violence who are economically exploited; c. children who do not have parents and are cared for by parties or families who are unable;
d. child victims of natural disasters or social disasters; and e. children with disabilities.
6.5.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes specific provisions for people with disabilities (children with disabilities) through an obligation to provide social welfare for children with disabilities, indicating targeted measures for persons with disabilities (though not specifically women with disabilities).

CHAPTER IV
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN


Part One Prevention of Acts of Violence against Women and Children

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Dharmasraya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Dharmasraya Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Dharmasraya.
4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Dharmasraya Regency.
5. Social Service, Women's Empowerment, Child Protection, Population Control and Family Planning, hereinafter referred to as the Service, is the Regional Apparatus that handles affairs in the Field of Implementation of Women's and Children's Protection.
6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and justice in a number of aspects of human life, through policies and programs that take into account the experiences, aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies and programs in various fields of life and development.
8. Gender Mainstreaming Working Group, hereinafter referred to as Pokja Gender Mainstreaming, is a consultation forum for implementers and drivers of gender mainstreaming from various agencies/institutions in the region.
9. Gender Mainstreaming Focal Point is an apparatus in the Regional Apparatus who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units.
10. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb.
11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Prevention is direct efforts made by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and children.
13. Children's Forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes concerning their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
14. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
15. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions taken by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is action by apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence.
25. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the soul through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
26. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
27. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
28. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
29. Customs are eternal and hereditary codes of conduct from one generation to another generation as heritage, so that they are strongly integrated with the behavioral patterns of society.

Article 64
The Regional Government is obligated to provide Social Welfare for:
a. children in conflict with the law; b. child victims of violence who are economically exploited; c. children who do not have parents and are cared for by parties or families who are unable;
d. child victims of natural disasters or social disasters; and e. children with disabilities.

Article 56
(1) Every organizer of an educational unit is obligated to provide opportunities to Children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
(2) Every organizer of an educational unit is prohibited from expelling Children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the Child's education.
(3) In the event that a Child victim of an act of Violence experiences dropping out of school, then the child victim of violence shall be provided formal or non-formal education, in this case carried out by the organizer of the educational unit and coordinated with the Women and Child Empowerment Unit

Article 58
(1) Children with disabilities and Children with special needs are given equal opportunities to obtain formal, nonformal and informal education services, including inclusive education programs.
(2) Regional governments provide teaching staff for inclusive education at every education unit.

6.5.rationale: The Indonesian text contains explicit disability-targeted provisions for children: Pasal 6 huruf l grants rights for children with disabilities/special needs; Pasal 58 mandates equal opportunities including inclusive education; Pasal 59(2)(b) includes fee waivers for “anak penyandang disabilitas”; and Pasal 64(e) obligates social welfare for “anak penyandang disabilitas.” Given these explicit measures, a ‘Yes’ for disability-related intersectional attention is supported, so the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect.
